🇲🇽🏭 <u>AGUASCALIENTES BREAKS 9-YEAR FDI RECORD — $342M, +211%</u>

Aguascalientes captured $342.1 million in direct foreign investment in Q1 2026, a 211.4% jump from Q1 2025 — the state's best first quarter in nine years, according to data released by Mexico's federal Secretaría de Economía per El Financiero.

Japan led with $144 million, Germany followed with $96.3M, and the United States came in third at $66.6M. Manufacturing alone absorbed $271.8M of the total, a 127% year-over-year jump. This builds on Mexico's national Q1 FDI record of $23.591 billion — the largest first quarter on record. Trump's tariff war, the credit-rating downgrades, the "investment flight" narrative: capital still bets on Mexico.

Source: El Financiero

🚨🇱🇧 <u>NYT INVESTIGATION CONFIRMS ISRAEL DROPPED WHITE PHOSPHORUS ON LEBANESE CIVILIANS</u>

A New York Times investigation corroborates video evidence of Israeli white phosphorus shells deployed in populated Lebanese areas — including Nabatieh (pop. ~40,000), Tiro, Qlayaa, Khiam, Yohmor and the Beaufort Castle zone, per Regeneración.

The M825A1 munitions each contain 116 felt wedges coated in white phosphorus that ignite automatically on contact with air — "extremadamente complicado de apagar" — and burn 5-10 minutes, scattering incendiary fragments. Use in civilian zones is a war crime under international humanitarian law. Israel's response: our guidelines say it "should not be used in high-density populated areas, except in specific situations." Even the Newspaper of Record can no longer hide what Mexico has named.

Source: Regeneración

🚨🇲🇽 <u>VERACRUZ JOURNALIST ROXANA GUZMÁN — TAKEN FROM HER HOME, SIX DAYS GONE</u>

Roxana Guzmán Ramírez, director of the digital portal Pulso Informativo del Sureste, was taken from her residence in Nanchital, southern Veracruz, on June 2 by an armed group. Six days later, no trace.

Governor Rocío Nahle García: "Desde el primer momento tanto la Fiscalía General del Estado de Veracruz como las fuerzas de seguridad federales, estatales y locales han estado buscando." Additional security reinforcements were sent to the south of the state; the State Attorney's office declined to release investigation details. Mexico remains the deadliest country on Earth for journalists outside an active war zone.

Source: Contralínea

🚨🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM GOVT OFFERS CNTE THE HEAD OF USICAMM</u>

Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez and Education Secretary Mario Delgado handed CNTE a concrete roadmap to dismantle USICAMM — the punitive teacher-evaluation institution born from Peña Nieto's 2013 educational reform — and to overhaul the 2007 ISSSTE pension law that gutted teacher retirements.

Timeline per Contralínea: June 15 working table; June 16-20 diagnostic phase; Aug 18-31 democratic teacher consultation; September 14 sent to Congress. "El gobierno federal mantiene abiertas las puertas del diálogo," Rodríguez said. Delgado: "Ya pasaron 19 meses y cada que nos reunimos: 'maestros hay que hacer la mesa.'" The neoliberal teaching architecture CNTE has fought for a decade — finally on the table.

Source: Contralínea

Her legal advisor — even on personal business matters — is Roberto Gil Zuarth, Calderón's former legislative coordinator.

Campos Galván "works only Wednesdays every other week, after noon" and skips state security meetings, the paper reports. Same governor who days ago hosted Vicente Fox and Calderón to denounce Morena for "handing power to the cartels." The narco-PAN dynasty refuses to die.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>BANKS POCKET RECORD 104 BILLION PESOS — Q1 2026 PROFITS BLOW PAST EVERY PRIOR YEAR</u>

Private banks operating in Mexico raked in 104.74 billion pesos in profits between January and April 2026 — the largest figure for that period since records exist, according to the CNBV. The eight systemically important banks — BBVA Mexico, Banorte, Santander, Banamex, Inbursa, Scotiabank, HSBC and Citi Mexico — alone took 87.87 billion, a 29.55% nominal jump from 67.83 billion in the same period of 2025.

The total credit portfolio of private banking reached 8.28 trillion pesos, just 1.94% higher in real terms. Profits explode; lending barely moves. Foreign banks. Mexican spreads. Working class pays.

Source: La Jornada
